subject: Renewal: Commit recalibration & uplift cap
messages:
From: Anna Lopez <anna@ledgerai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@ledgerai.com
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Commit tiers for Hosted API renewal

Marissa —

Thanks for the renewal notice. We're evaluating our usage and want to avoid a big overcommit this cycle. Current Q4 usage spiked because of a POC; baseline for production looks closer to ~250M tokens/month, but we do have predictable bursts tied to marketing campaigns.

Two asks from procurement:
- Can we get a tighter uplift cap at renewal (we're comfortable with a 20% uplift rather than unlimited or 2x)?
- Is there a path to a stepped commit that lets us scale to higher tiers mid-year without an immediate penalty?

Can you share a model of what a right-sized commit + uplift cap would look like on per-token pricing?

Anna
Anna Lopez
Head of Cloud Integrations, LedgerAI
anna@ledgerai.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@ledgerai.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-23T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit tiers for Hosted API renewal

Anna —

Thanks for the clear direction. Attached is an initial model (ledger_commit_modeling.xlsx) showing three commit profiles: Conserved (250M/mo), Growth (400M/mo with burst capacity), and Aggressive (700M/mo). Key points:

- Per-token list price stays the same; discounts scale with committed monthly token volumes.
- We can lock an uplift cap at 20% at renewal if you commit to the Conserved or Growth tier. For Aggressive tier we typically allow a 25% uplift cap.
- We offer a mid-term re-tier option: a one-time reseat of commit (up or down) after month 6 with pro-rated pricing adjustments and no additional uplift fees, provided total paid commit stays within 15% of original over the 12-month term.

If that one-time mid-term reseat sounds useful I can flag it as part of the contract and ask Legal to add language. Sean — fyi on the reseat mechanics; can you weigh in on the acceptable commercial guardrails?

Attachment: ledger_commit_modeling.xlsx (xlsx)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Lopez <anna@ledgerai.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Commit tiers for Hosted API renewal

Marissa — quick note from commercial/legal side:

- The one-time mid-term reseat is reasonable commercially, but I recommend we cap the reseat delta at +/- 25% to avoid churny churn (we've seen customers oscillate).
- For renewal uplift limits, Legal prefers a numeric cap rather than percentage when possible (easier to audit). Suggest: "uplift cap = committed monthly tokens + 20%" and include an example table in the SOW.
- We should also include an express clause that refunds or true-ups are based on billed usage vs. committed token amounts monthly.

Grace — can you please prepare the SOW language for the uplift table and the reseat clause?

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Cloud Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal: Right-sizing commit + 20% uplift cap (updated)

Anna —

Attached is the updated proposal (Redwood_Pricing_Proposal_Marissa_v2.pdf). Highlights:

1) Recommended tier: Growth — 400M committed tokens/month. Discount schedule in the PDF shows a stepped per-token discount that improves at 500M and 700M thresholds; you only pay the lower per-token rate for tokens inside the higher tranche.
2) Renewal uplift language: we agree to a 20% uplift cap on committed monthly tokens at renewal for the Growth tier. Example added to SOW: if committed = 400M, uplift cap = 480M.
3) Mid-term reseat: one-time reseat allowed after month 6; cap +/- 25% of original commit. Reseat requires 30 days' notice and will adjust invoice starting the following billing cycle.
4) No fees for moving up tiers mid-term; moving down mid-term triggers pro-rated adjustments to remaining term with a small administrative fee (0.5% of remaining committed value).
